svg.title: Frontier Wars, Van Diemen’s Land & The Victorian Gold Rush (1803–1854)
svg.desc: KS3 Year 8 historical GIS atlas map of Eastern and South-Eastern Australia (1803–1854) showing accurate 1851–1854 colonial boundaries (New South Wales without the post-1859 Queensland border, the 1851 Colony of Victoria along the Murray River, South Australia west of 141°E, and Van Diemen’s Land), highlighting Crossing the Blue Mountains and Bathurst (1813–24), the June 1838 Myall Creek Massacre, Ballarat and the December 1854 Eureka Stockade, and a zoomed Van Diemen’s Land and Flinders Island GIS inset detailing the Black War, Governor Arthur’s 1830 Black Line, and the Wybalenna exile.

g.text: ZOOM: VAN DIEMEN’S LAND, BLACK LINE & FLINDERS ISLAND (1803–35)

text.tspan: Oyster Bay & Big River nations resist

svg.text: KS3 HISTORY • YEAR 8 ENQUIRY: FIRST NATIONS & COLONIAL AUSTRALIA
Frontier Wars, Van Diemen’s Land & The Victorian Gold Rush (1803–1854)
Booming Yorkshire demand for Merino wool drove squatters across inland Country, sparking martial law and frontier massacres.
While Van Diemen’s Land waged the Black War (1826–30), Victoria’s 1851 Gold Rush & 1854 Eureka Stockade won white male suffrage.
